properties.description:
The five guarded constructors (add_requirement, add_capability, add_component, add_decision, add_design_rule) take `replaces: [<old id>]`, and the same-type near-match refusal names THREE routes: sharpen, distinct_from, replaces. For each replaced node (reflow2_core::supersede): (1) its ending is recorded FIRST — a `deprecation` ChangeEvent chg:replaced:<old>:by:<new> that `removed` it from the live design, pinned to the standing preserve epoch, whose snapshot keeps its properties AND edges; (2) the edges that say what it was FOR move to the successor — a Capability's SATISFIES, the ALLOCATED_TO pointing at a Component, nothing for the other three types (a requirement's satisfiers are a delivery claim nobody made again); (3) the successor OBSOLETES it, with evidence. Every other design edge stays on the old node and is NAMED in the reply (`replaced[].stays_on_replaced`), and `standing` says, read from the graph, what still withdraws it: an ACCEPTED Decision that OBSOLETES it (so an accepted successor Decision withdraws its predecessor at once), or for a requirement `dropped` on the owner's word. The old node's stored status never moves. Works on a revise, so a successor recorded earlier can be joined later. Refused, nothing written: an id of another type (a record at another layer is not a predecessor), one naming nothing, one also in distinct_from, the node itself.

`distinct_from` is written onto the node the call created (a list:string property on Requirement, Capability, Component, Decision, DesignRule and Constraint), merged with any earlier judgement; an id naming nothing is reported in `judged_distinct.not_recorded`, never kept.

WHY THIS EDGE: OBSOLETES from the successor is what retire-from-design names for a Capability/Component with a successor and what dec:reopen-supersedes uses; SUPERSEDES is declared for Fragment/Verification only and its survival is dec:one-retire-edge's open question; EVOLVES_INTO is the promotion edge. WHY A PROPERTY for distinct_from: no schema edge says "compared, not the same", and the design's precedent for a recorded judgement that is not a relation is no_relation_note.
properties.name: A capture tool can say its new node REPLACES an older one — the old node's ending is recorded, its thread moves, the new node OBSOLETES it — and a distinct_from judgement is kept on the node it created
